chapter: Lover Man and the postwar years
title: Jimmy Davis, the Army and Lady Sings the Blues
summary: Jimmy Davis was drafted and pitched Billie Holiday; she wrote of him in her book, implying Ramirez did not write the song.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Now, when Jimmy got in the Army, we me... And we were conscientious objectors. They took us back and forth, back and forth, you know. They came to the time that they didn't ask you "Do you believe in war?" They just took you. But Jimmy had to go in, and I went into Special Service, USO, you know. Well, by the time... I had the in already, you know, with the band, and he had this uniform on, and he would solicit Billie Holiday, and he had... Jimmy has a

winsome personality, a beautiful personality. This is why she wrote in her book, Lady Sings The Blues, "Poor Jimmy, he hasn't got a (?) in the world. Jimmy will cry!" -- when things get rough, you know. Well, anyway, he didn't need to do that, because it was already in the cards, and she was supposed to record the number.

Anyway, he became a warrant officer, and... Well, she did, and she wrote about him in Lady Sings The Blues. Well, she has so many suits about her in that book that, I mean, I didn't bother. I said, "Look, John, she's inferring that I didn't write this song." He said, "Well, look, they got so many suits..."
